## Session Report

* [H-D1 report: MadGraph sums the two decay assignments of one subprocess incoherently; their interference is below 1e-3](H-D1-report.md) - On the pinned checkout, one subprocess reached by two disjoint decay assignments becomes two matrix elements (or two PDF terms of one), so MadEvent sums |M_a|² + |M_b|², each inside its own Breit–Wigner window; measured on p p > z j j, z > j j (30 such subprocesses, the same 30 vibegraph refuses, diagram totals equal). With vibegraph's own evaluators the interference is ≤ 1.4e-3 ± 1.1e-3 (colour-aligned e+ e-), 3.5e-4 (g g) and exactly 0 (q q̄ initial). A coherent sum differs from MadGraph mainly through the window union (+0.24% to +1.1%) and through cut_decays = F, where it moves σ by −23% to −26% or is IR-unsafe. Recommendation: match MadGraph. Neither option unblocks the hadronic cards alone: both then stop at the per-group cut-filter refusal.
* [H-G0 report: why crossing pairs refuse a shared colour basis](H-G0-report.md) - The charge-conjugate pairs have one basis up to a permutation, and the raw-order CF check refuses them before flow_permutation, which finds it, can run. The Singlet-model refusal is 184 zero-coupling b-Yukawa diagrams in the member.
* [H-G1 report: conjugate pairs share one flavour group under the flow permutation](H-G1-report.md) - The review of colour-split-groups, then the manager's scope update: colour_pairing takes π from the fingerprints and checks the CF matrix under π, so conjugate pairs form one group and only genuinely unpaired subprocesses (d d > d d / b b > b b at a zero b Yukawa) split.
